headline: NHS genetic test slashes childhood cancer diagnosis time from weeks to days
meta_description: A rapid NHS genetic test is cutting cancer diagnosis time for children from 4-6 weeks to 2-3 days, sparing some from unnecessary invasive treatment.
summary_short: A Cambridge study shows a rapid NHS genetic test can diagnose childhood tumors in 2-3 days instead of 4-6 weeks, helping avoid unnecessary procedures.
body:
A rapid NHS genetic test is cutting cancer diagnosis time for children from 4 to 6 weeks down to just 2 to 3 days. In a Cambridge study, the speedier results had immediate impact: two children avoided invasive treatment for benign tumours, sparing them unnecessary procedures and hospital time.

Faster diagnosis means faster answers for families waiting in uncertainty. When results that once took over a month arrive in days, clinicians can quickly determine which tumors are benign and require only monitoring, rather than rushing into surgery based on incomplete information.

The study demonstrates how targeted genetic testing—rather than traditional diagnostic methods—can both accelerate care and improve outcomes. By identifying tumor characteristics rapidly and accurately, the NHS test allows doctors to tailor treatment decisions precisely to each child's needs.
quick_facts: Test time reduced from 4-6 weeks to 2-3 days
Two children avoided unnecessary invasive treatment
Identified benign tumors requiring monitoring only
